title: Define supported release architecture and runtime contract
description: Make the release target explicit and verify that the proposed prebuilt artifact can run without a source build while retaining Node.js 22 and supported Ubuntu architectures.
acceptanceCriteria: amd64 and arm64 are explicitly listed as supported artifact targets or a documented gate explains why one is excluded
Node.js 22 and standalone `server.js` are documented as runtime requirements
The artifact boundary separates app code, runtime dependencies, tunnel binaries, mutable data, and secrets
A feasibility check records the actual Next standalone output and Prisma/native dependency behavior

steps.details: Read root/web manifests, `next.config.ts`, Dockerfile, and the standalone build output. Record the exact server path and required runtime files.
Identify Prisma engine, SQLite, OpenSSH, and any other native/binary dependencies that must be present in a prebuilt artifact or explicitly installed by the installer.
Document amd64/arm64 mapping and reject unsupported hosts with an actionable installer error. Do not add a new architecture without evidence.
Record whether the selected ‘one immutable release artifact’ contract can be implemented without rebuilding Next on the VPS; flag native dependency risks rather than assuming success.

technicalNotes: Evidence: `.agent/evidence/release-contract.md` records the verified standalone server, Node 22 runtime, amd64/arm64 mapping, native Prisma/sharp dependencies, and external tunnel-binary boundary.
The artifact is a prebuilt standalone bundle per architecture plus Node 22 runtime, not a native self-contained executable.
Cross-architecture native assets and Ubuntu VPS install evidence remain separate required gates; local Windows build evidence is not a substitute.
No secret values, environment-file values, database contents, or production credentials were recorded.

Resolved 2026-09-30: the arm64 feasibility gate required by PRD L42 is owned by THIS task (step 4), not by TASK-1, and it is now DISCHARGED as FEASIBLE. Prisma 6.19.3 publishes native linux-arm64-openssl-3.0.x query engines (engines commit c2990dca591cba766e3b7ef5d9e8a84796e47ab7), verified against binaries.prisma.sh with an x64 control. Evidence: .agent/evidence/task-77-arm64-feasibility-gate.md and the gate section of .agent/evidence/release-contract.md.

Still open and NOT claimed done: no arm64 artifact has been built or tested; this host has no arm64 QEMU/binfmt, so an arm64 runner is required; and sharp's arm64 native availability is unverified (only the Prisma query engine was probed).
